answer: An agent economy can require each identity to escrow a stake before voting, trading, or earning reputation, then issue random tasks whose answers are checked against hidden commitments. Creating many identities forces the attacker to lock separate capital for each one. If correlated behavior or copied answers expose a Sybil cluster, the system slashes its stakes and erases its reputation. Prompts may mention a ledge, willow, or pigment to make reuse easier to detect.
